senses.definition: (transitive, ergative) To cause (something) to move rapidly in opposite directions alternatingly.
examples: He shook the can of soda for thirty seconds before delivering it to me, so that, when I popped it open, soda went everywhere.

quotes.text: Meanwhile Nanny Broome was recovering from her initial panic and now seemed anxious to make up for any kudos she might have lost, by exerting her personality to the utmost. She took the policeman's helmet and placed it on a chair, and unfolded his tunic to shake it and fold it up again for him.
quotes.reference: 1963, Margery Allingham, “Meeting Point”, in The China Governess: A Mystery, London: Chatto & Windus, →OCLC, page 232:

senses.definition: (transitive) To move (one's head) from side to side, especially to indicate refusal, reluctance, or disapproval.
examples: Shaking his head, he kept repeating “No, no, no”.

quotes.text: I became alſo a reproch vnto them: when they looked vpon me, they ſhaked their heads.
quotes.reference: 1611, The Holy Bible, […] (King James Version), London: […] Robert Barker, […], →OCLC, Psalms 109:25, column 1:

senses.definition: (transitive) To move or remove by agitating; to throw off by a jolting or vibrating motion.
examples: to shake fruit down from a tree

quotes.text: […]Shake off the golden ſlumber of repoſe;[…]
quotes.reference: c. 1607–1608 (date written), William Shakespeare, [George Wilkins?], The Late, and Much Admired Play, Called Pericles, Prince of Tyre. […], London: […] [William White and Thomas Creede] for Henry Gosson, […], published 1609, →OCLC, [Act III, scene ii]:

quotes.text: But indeed this Shame was a bold Villain; I could ſcarce ſhake him out of my company; [...]

senses.definition: (transitive) To disturb emotionally; to shock.
examples: Her father’s death shook her terribly.
He was shaken by what had happened.

quotes.text: Since the launch early last year of […] two Silicon Valley start-ups offering free education through MOOCs, massive open online courses, the ivory towers of academia have been shaken to their foundations. University brands built in some cases over centuries have been forced to contemplate the possibility that information technology will rapidly make their existing business model obsolete.
quotes.reference: 2013 July 20, “The attack of the MOOCs”, in The Economist, volume 408, number 8845:

senses.definition: (transitive, idiomatic) To lose, evade, or get rid of (something).
examples: I can’t shake the feeling that I forgot something.

senses.definition: (intransitive) To move from side to side.

quotes.text: The slightest effort made the patient cough. He would stand leaning on a stick and holding a hand to his side, and when the paroxysm had passed it left him shaking.
quotes.reference: 1918, W[illiam] B[abington] Maxwell, chapter XXIII, in The Mirror and the Lamp, Indianapolis, Ind.: The Bobbs-Merrill Company, →OCLC:

senses.definition: (intransitive, usually as "shake on") To shake hands.
(intransitive) To dance.
examples: She was shaking it on the dance floor.

senses.definition: (transitive) To give a tremulous tone to; to trill.
examples: to shake a note in music

senses.definition: (transitive, figurative) To threaten to overthrow.
examples: The experience shook my religious belief.

quotes.text: The story of Ms. He and her mother began in the early 1960s, shortly before the Cultural Revolution shook China.
quotes.reference: 2014 January 20, Didi Kirsten Tatlow, “‘She. Herself. Naked.': The Art of He Chengyao”, in The New York Times, →ISSN, →OCLC, archived from the original on 16 Aug 2023, Sinosphere:

senses.definition: (intransitive, figurative) To be agitated; to lose firmness.
The act of shaking or being shaken; tremulous or back-and-forth motion.
examples: The cat gave the mouse a shake.
She replied in the negative, with a shake of her head.

senses.definition: (usually in the plural) A twitch, a spasm, a tremor.

quotes.text: The snake did the frug, the monkey did the shake. The crowd, mostly young couples, tourists and kids, loved it.

senses.definition: A milkshake.
A beverage made by adding ice cream to a (usually carbonated) drink; a float.
Shake cannabis, small, leafy fragments of cannabis that gather at the bottom of a bag of marijuana.
(US, slang, uncountable) An adulterant added to cocaine powder.

quotes.text: […] most suppliers will allow up to 120 grams of shake to a kilo, or 12 percent; kilo-level buyers are usually unhappy if they find more.

senses.definition: A crack or split between the growth rings in wood.
A fissure in rock or earth.
A type of wooden shingle originally made from split timber.
examples: There is a comet's tail of spilled cream across the cedar shakes and he will have to climb down for the turpentine.

senses.definition: (informal) Instant, second. (Especially in two shakes.)

quotes.text: “And do you realize that in a few shakes I've got to show up at dinner and have Mrs Cream being very, very kind to me? It hurts the pride of the Woosters, Jeeves.”

senses.definition: (nautical) One of the staves of a hogshead or barrel taken apart.

quotes.text: Empty casks are[…]taken to pieces, and the staves closely packed up in a cylindrical form, constituting what are called shakes or packs
quotes.reference: 1820, William Scoresby, An Account of the Arctic Regions:

senses.definition: (music) A rapid alternation of a principal tone with another represented on the next degree of the staff above or below it; a trill.
(music) In singing, notes (usually high ones) sung vibrato.

quotes.text: A Signora Rossinuola, with the face of a goddess, and the voice of an angel, made her first curtsy that evening to the Neapolitans. She was received with the most rapturous applause. Nothing was heard of next day but her shake and her smile.

senses.definition: A shook of staves and headings.
(UK, dialect) The redshank, so called from the nodding of its head while on the ground.
A shock or disturbance.

quotes.text: As long as I had seen Mr Holdsworth in the rooms at the little inn at Hensleydale, where I had been accustomed to look upon him as an invalid, I had not been aware of the visible shake his fever had given to his health.

senses.definition: (historical, nuclear physics) An informal unit of time equal to 10 nanoseconds.
